elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as rendered retains automatic annual renewal ("This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date") and no mutual-written-agreement renewal mechanic was inserted; the conditional automatic-renewal elements (30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder) are not all satisfied, so this element is not excused.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Retained language: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — a 12-month renewal term.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered text requires "written notice to the other given at least 60 days in advance" — a 60-day opt-out obligation, exceeding the 30-day preferred ceiling.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation on HDI appears anywhere in the rendered operative language; the 60-day reminder is mentioned only in the margin comment as a preference, which is not operative.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: consideration is fixed in Section 3.1 as "thirty percent (3016) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month" and neither Section 3.1 nor Section 4.1 grants HDI any right to increase pricing on renewal, so no uplift cap is triggered.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Operative edit replaces "upon ninety (90) days written notice" with "upon written notice to the other given at least 60 days in advance", read against the retained next sentence ("Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated"), yielding a 60-day window. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a pattern artifact (it expects the "sixty (60) days" word-and-numeral form); the numeral 60 is present and substantively caps the window at 60 days.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not triggered — pricing is a fixed 30% Net Sales revenue share under Section 3.1 with no renewal-uplift right in Section 4.1, so there is no price increase to cap.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the notice window is reset from 90 to 60 days in operative text, and the price-cap element is untriggered because the Agreement contains no renewal price-uplift right (fixed 30% Net Sales share in Section 3.1).

Preferred remains incomplete for three independent reasons — the opt-out is 60 days rather than ≤30, there is no operative HDI reminder obligation 60 days before renewal, and renewal stays automatic rather than by mutual written agreement. The reminder is only promised in the margin comment, which is not operative.

Minimality holds: the edit touches only the notice-period phrase within the same sentence and retains the favourable mutual "either Party" exit right, the one-year renewal term, the anniversary mechanic and the "Termination Date" definition. No survival tail, procedure or extra obligation was added.

Intent is preserved: the "Termination Date" definition still has its defining sentence, the notice-content requirement still operates, and Section 3.1 economics are untouched; no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence results.

Drafting polish (non-blocking): conform the inserted period to house style and pin the anchor explicitly, e.g. "upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other" or "at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term", so the "in advance" anchor does not rely on the following sentence and the deterministic window check reads cleanly.
